Visit note | 2025-01-22 11:00 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Nazmul Gazi, 53, male. The patient presents with highly itchy, dry patches on his elbows and knees, which cause him to scratch intensely at night. He works as a tailor and reports that these symptoms have become worse since switching to a strong detergent in Sylhet. He has no other known chronic medical conditions. On physical examination: affected area about 4 cm across, BP 117/85 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 81 kg. The skin lesions are dry, erythematous, and excoriated. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Visit note | 2025-01-22 03:30 PM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Mahfuz Sarkar, 21, male. The patient presents with high fever, pain behind the eyes, and severe aching in his bones and muscles. He is a university student and states that these symptoms started after a week of stagnant rainwater around his house in Chattogram. He has no prior comorbidities. Visit note | 2025-01-22 03:30 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Liton Gazi, 64, male. The patient presents to the clinic complaining of feeling increasingly slow and tired over the past several months, accompanied by unexplained weight gain and dry skin. He works as a madrasa teacher. He explains that these symptoms were investigated and found during diagnostic tests for tiredness after he recently moved to Rampura. He denies any chest pain, palpitations, cold intolerance, or changes in bowel habits, though he notes some generalized sluggishness. He has no other known chronic medical conditions or comorbidities, and he does not take any regular medications. On physical examination: TSH 12.5 mIU/L, BP 136/73 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 86 kg. The patient is alert, cooperative, and oriented, though his speech and movements appear slightly slow. His skin is noticeably dry and cool to the touch, and there is mild non-pitting puffiness around his eyes. Chest examination reveals normal breath sounds, and cardiovascular examination shows a regular rhythm with normal S1 and S2. Abdominal examination is soft and non-tender with normal bowel sounds. No thyroid enlargement or nodules are palpable in the neck. Sensation and reflexes are intact in all four limbs, though the relaxation phase of his deep tendon reflexes is slightly delayed. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. The clinical presentation and laboratory findings indicate primary hypothyroidism, and thyroid hormone replacement therapy is initiated today. The patient was educated on the importance of taking his medication daily on an empty stomach. He was advised to keep a regular sleep routine and to eat a balanced diet to support his general health and energy levels. He was also instructed to monitor for any symptoms of hyperthyroidism, such as palpitations or excessive sweating, and to report them immediately. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH to monitor progress and adjust the dosage if necessary.
